title: Scaffolded Codex vs naked Codex: compact evolution handoff
question: For a bounded cold-resume evolution-loop decision, does Open Scaffold give Codex the same or better decision quality with a lighter/faster prompt than a naked raw-artifact prompt?

control.label: Naked Codex over raw loop artifacts

scaffolded.label: Open Scaffold compact evolution controller signal + Codex

metrics.label: Median rubric score for next-action decision
metrics.notes: Quality tied at 5/5 median; the scaffolded arm did not trade quality away for compactness.

metrics.label: Decision quality per 1k Codex-reported tokens
metrics.notes: Derived from median 5/5 quality and Codex-reported total tokens.

metrics.label: Prompt payload bytes given to Codex
metrics.notes: Direct payload size, not an inferred model-token count.

metrics.label: Median total tokens reported by Codex CLI
metrics.notes: Three read-only replicates per arm; medians are used because individual Codex token receipts were noisy.

metrics.label: Median wall-clock seconds for Codex response
metrics.notes: Wall time includes Codex CLI overhead on the local machine.

metrics.label: Evolution loop accepted-criteria gain from baseline to frontier
metrics.notes: The Open Scaffold loop records a rejected regressing attempt and a promoted frontier that moves the fixture from 2/3 to 3/3 accepted criteria.

caveats: Bounded fixture proof only: one cold-resume evolution-loop decision task, not all AI work.
Codex CLI total-token receipts were noisy across replicates; prompt payload bytes and medians are reported separately instead of hidden.
Open Scaffold did not spawn Codex in this proof; Codex was run manually/read-only and the framework evaluated source-labeled receipts.
The evolution delta comes from the checked-in evolution-ledger demo, not from claiming this run made a model smarter.
